HR@10 with one positive and 99 unique negatives measures success within 100 candidates. Krichene and Rendle show that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation. Identical users and candidates support controlled benchmark comparisons, but uniqueness and fixed seeds do not remove sampling bias. Report gains explicitly as sampled-candidate HR@10; they do not establish better full-catalog top-10 retrieval. [On Sampled Metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For this four-dataset design, report each dataset’s HR@10 and paired absolute improvement, plus their equally weighted macro-average. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. A suitable uncertainty analysis, following paired retrieval-evaluation methods, resamples users within each dataset while keeping both models’ outcomes paired, then recomputes the macro difference for a 95% bootstrap interval. Include discordant counts—users helped versus harmed. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the four datasets, fixed candidates and fitted models; they exclude training and candidate-resampling variability and generalization to new datasets. [Paired evaluation methods](https://ciir-publications.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744)

Repeatedly selecting architectures, hyperparameters or checkpoints on the same validation users creates adaptive selection bias: the winning validation gain is optimistic. Ordinary paired intervals or p-values computed after selection do not correct that bias. Disclose the search budget, trials and selection rule; treat validation gains as exploratory. Freeze the final choice before the host’s independent held-out evaluation. That evaluation can substantiate generalization under the pinned sampled-candidate protocol, while full-catalog claims still require full-catalog evidence. [Adaptive holdout reuse](https://research.google/blog/the-reusable-holdout-preserving-validity-in-adaptive-data-analysis/)
